messages:
devon: heads up — paging integration to PagerRelay is failing for the last 11m. several customer pages didn't reach oncall.
alex: seeing it, getting 410s from the relay endpoint.
maria: oh no — did the signing key rotate?
devon: not ours. logs show payload accepted but relay returns 410 / disposition: duplicate. looks new.
katie: oncall didn't get SMS/VPN push either. manual paging kicked off.
sre-bot: incident detected: notify-orch webhook error rate > 5/min (alerting).
alex: dumping sample request/response:
```
POST /v1/pagerrelays/ingest HTTP/1.1
Host: relay.redwood-internal.net
X-Signature: sha256=...
{
  "alert_id":"A-2321",
  "dest":"sms:REDACTED",
  "body":"prod latency spike"
}
--- RESPONSE ---
HTTP/1.1 410 Gone
{ "error": "duplicate_event", "relay_id": "R-998" }
```
alex: the relay used to dedupe by external_id; our payloads include a transient request_id. suspect their parse of external_id regressed.
maria: can we change our outbound to include a monotonic external_id as workaround?
devon: quick mitigation: switching to manual-fanout for affected alerts (SMS + call) while we work with PagerRelay. kicked the automation off.
katie: manual pages sent for 4 impacted customers. ops oncall acknowledged.
alex: reached out to PagerRelay support — they admitted a recent deploy changed dedupe key from `external_id` to `signature_id`. they're rolling a fix. ETA 30m.
maria: in parallel we should add a compatibility header so they can map `request_id -> external_id`. can we ship a quick relay shim?
devon: I can flip a proxy config in edge for the notify-orch to copy `request_id` into `external_id` header. will do a canary for 10% first.
sre-bot: change requested: notify-orch/proxy add header X-External-Id = request_id (canary 10%).
alex: devon, when you flip canary, pls post curl to test.
devon: flipping now. pushing config...
devon: canary up at 10%. testing with synthetic alert.
alex: test result — relay responded 202 Accepted and created page. good.
katie: confirming oncall received SMS for the test.
maria: great. should we keep canary and expand?
devon: will hold 10% for 15m to watch for any side effects, then 100% if stable.
alex: PagerRelay says they deployed revert. they recommend we still add compatibility header as belt+brace.
devon: noted. follow-up tasks: 1) keep canary 15m 2) rollout header 100% if no regressions 3) postmortem draft + customer impact list 4) contact CS for affected customers.
katie: customer impact: 4 customers had delayed pages; one had a support ticket opened. ops already notified CS lead.
maria: starting postmortem skeleton now — will include timeline, root cause (relay dedupe key change), mitigation (proxy header), and long-term: signed schema contract.
devon: leaving this thread for ops-runbook updates. ping me if any further failures. :thumbsup:
pager-relay-bot: automated note: Relay deploy id d-2026-03-18 detected. revert initiated at 1755552400.
alex: closing loop — canary healthy, relay reverted. last impacted alert timestamp 1755551100. follow-ups in #postmortems.
katie: thanks all, great run.
